question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's restart-specific durable SQLite audit table and 512-row redacted metadata retention boundary once the branch is rebased onto current main?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a narrow code defect; it is an intentional persisted-state, privacy, and restart-availability contract that automation should not accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept After Rebase
options.body: Preserve current-main gateway reload behavior during rebase, then accept the new restart audit table, metadata fields, retention cap, and post-transition write placement as the intended operator audit boundary.

options.title: Narrow Persisted Metadata
options.body: Require a smaller column/context set or stricter redaction policy before merging the durable audit table.

options.title: Pause For Broader Ledger
options.body: Defer this restart-specific producer if maintainers want all local audit records to land through a broader audit-ledger design instead.

recommendation.title: Accept After Rebase
recommendation.body: Preserve current-main gateway reload behavior during rebase, then accept the new restart audit table, metadata fields, retention cap, and post-transition write placement as the intended operator audit boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears repeatedly in the feature history for restart deferral and gateway restart control-plane behavior, which makes him the best available product-boundary owner from the history checked.
